text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential, because it helps developers understand how to use your API quickly. In addition, you should plan for versioning from the beginning, for example by including /v1/ in your URLs. This makes it easier to update the API later without breaking existing applications. Following these simple rules will make your API easier to use and maintain.
